key_insight: Choosing the R or S enantiomer reverses polarization and persistent spin direction in polar chiral two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a route to molecularly selected spin control for spintronic devices, rather than a demonstrated improvement in solar-cell performance.
method: Derived symmetry-allowed spin–orbit fields for the polar P2₁ crystal structure.
Calculated first-principles spin textures for ten compounds, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues.
Ranked 34 two-band k·p models by spin-direction agreement rather than band energies.
evidence_signal: In strongly polar compounds, the persistent-term model achieved spin agreement ≥0.98 versus 0.20 for the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model, with coupling strengths of 1.09–1.98 eV Å.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational predictions, not experimental validation of spin persistence, device operation or photovoltaic efficiency gains.
paper_title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
